author: Wired

title: Apple Temporarily Removes Telegram from App Store
content:
Apple's Removal of Telegram from App Store Raises Questions on Moderation Policies

In a recent incident, Telegram, a popular messaging app used by over 1 billion users worldwide, temporarily vanished from Apple's App Store. The app's disappearance, which lasted for roughly an hour, has sparked renewed debate about Apple's moderation policies and how it handles different companies. According to Apple, Telegram was removed due to the presence of child sexual abuse material (CSAM), which was subsequently removed, and the app was reinstated.

The incident has highlighted the complexities of content moderation on app stores, particularly when it comes to balancing the need to protect users from harm with the need to respect freedom of expression. Apple's decision to remove Telegram has been met with criticism from some quarters, with some arguing that the company's moderation policies are inconsistent and unfairly target certain companies. The incident has also raised questions about the role of technology companies in policing online content and the challenges of enforcing moderation policies across different platforms.

The controversy surrounding Telegram's removal from the App Store is the latest in a series of high-profile incidents that have highlighted the need for greater transparency and consistency in app store moderation policies. As the tech industry continues to evolve, these issues are likely to remain a pressing concern for both companies and regulators, and will require ongoing debate and discussion to resolve.
author: The Verge

title: Min Aung Hlaing Seeks Legitimacy in Thailand
content:
Bangkok welcomed Myanmar’s former junta chief, Min Aung Hlaing, with a formal reception at the Thai embassy in Yangon earlier this week. The ceremony, attended by senior Thai officials and representatives from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), was described by the Thai foreign ministry as a “step toward constructive engagement.” Hlaing arrived in a private jet, was greeted with a red‑carpeted welcome, and met with Thai Deputy Foreign Minister Piyaporn Kittisak and ASEAN envoy Tuan Khalid.

Despite the cordial reception, experts caution that Hlaing’s prospects for regional acceptance remain limited. International sanctions imposed by the United States, the European Union, and several ASEAN members continue to restrict his travel and financial transactions. Moreover, the Myanmar military’s ongoing human‑rights violations and the lack of a credible transition plan have eroded trust among neighboring states. Analysts note that ASEAN’s “non‑interference” principle is being tested, and many member countries are reluctant to extend diplomatic recognition to a regime that has been widely condemned for its crackdown on civilians.

In short, while Thailand’s hospitality signals a willingness to engage, the former junta chief still faces significant diplomatic and economic hurdles that could impede his ability to secure full regional acceptance.
author: DW World

title: TPLF, Fano militias and Eritrea reshape northern Ethiopia conflict
content:
The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), local Fano militias, and Eritrean forces are reshaping the frontlines in northern Ethiopia, according to reports from the region’s security officials. Recent skirmishes along the Tigray‑Eritrea border have seen the TPLF consolidate control over key towns in the Amhara and Afar regions, while the Fano militias—primarily Amhara volunteers—have advanced into areas previously held by the TPLF. Eritrean troops, which entered the conflict in late 2020, are now reportedly moving deeper into Tigrayan territory, supporting the Ethiopian National Defense Forces (ENDF) in a coordinated push against the TPLF.

This realignment follows a series of ceasefire agreements that have largely stalled, with both sides accusing each other of violating terms. Analysts note that the TPLF’s strategic gains in the north could allow it to secure supply routes and cut off ENDF and Fano supply lines, potentially shifting the balance of power. Meanwhile, the involvement of Eritrean forces has raised concerns among neighboring countries and international observers about the potential for a broader regional conflict. The Ethiopian government has warned that any escalation could destabilize the fragile peace that has been in place since the 2022 peace accords.

In the coming weeks, observers will be watching for further troop movements and diplomatic negotiations that could either cement the new frontlines or prompt renewed talks. The situation remains fluid, with the potential for both a military stalemate and a negotiated settlement depending on the actions of the TPLF, the Fano militias, and Eritrean forces.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Shakib Al Hasan to face Bangladesh trial if safety assured, World Cup return planned
content:
Dhaka – Former captain and all‑rounder Shakib Al Hasan, a close ally of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, has indicated he will submit to a pending criminal trial in Bangladesh provided that the authorities guarantee his personal safety. The case, which stems from allegations of financial misconduct linked to a sports promotion venture, has been postponed repeatedly amid concerns over potential threats to the high‑profile athlete. Government officials have said they are preparing protective measures, while the judiciary has urged a swift resolution to avoid further disruption to the nation’s cricketing calendar.

The cricketer’s legal situation coincides with Bangladesh’s preparations for the upcoming ICC Cricket World Cup, where Shakib is expected to play a pivotal role in the national side’s campaign. The Bangladesh Cricket Board has expressed optimism that a secure environment will enable Shakib to rejoin the squad ahead of the tournament, emphasizing the importance of his experience for the team’s performance. Authorities remain focused on balancing the enforcement of the law with the need to maintain the country’s sporting interests, and a decision on the trial’s schedule is anticipated in the coming weeks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: China launches its first school for robots
content:
Beijing, China – The Chinese government announced the opening of the nation’s first dedicated robot school on Monday, a specialized institution aimed at advancing artificial intelligence and robotics research. The school, officially named the Institute of Robotic Cognition, will operate under the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, with an initial enrollment of 200 undergraduate and graduate students. “Our main goal is to empower robots’ brains,” said Dr. Li Wei, the institute’s director, emphasizing a curriculum that integrates machine learning, neural network design, sensor integration, and autonomous decision‑making.

The institute will collaborate with leading domestic technology firms, including Huawei, Baidu, and DJI, as well as international partners such as the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence. Funding of 1.2 billion yuan has been allocated for state‑of‑the‑art laboratories, high‑performance computing clusters, and pilot projects that test robotic systems in manufacturing, healthcare, and urban infrastructure. Officials expect the school to produce a new generation of engineers capable of developing more adaptable and intelligent robotic platforms, positioning China at the forefront of global robotics innovation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Tottenham and Atlético in talks over Romero with Van de Ven set to sign new deal
content:
Tottenham Hotspur are reportedly engaged in negotiations with Atlético Madrid over the transfer of defender Cristian Romero. The Argentina international had been linked with a move to Internazionale, but Atlético are now believed to be his preferred destination, with Diego Simeone's side willing to match the £35m bid initially offered by the Italian club. Romero has been at the center of transfer speculation for some time, having signed a four-year contract with Spurs at the start of last season but subsequently expressing his desire to leave the club.

Despite categorically rejecting an approach from Arsenal, Tottenham are now in talks with Atlético over the sale of Romero. The negotiations come as the North London club are also on the verge of agreeing a new deal with defender Micky van de Ven. The 22-year-old is expected to pen a five-year extension with Spurs, providing a much-needed boost to the club's defensive unit. Van de Ven has been a key player for the team this season, and the new contract will see him commit his future to the club.

The developments suggest a busy transfer window for Tottenham, with the club seeking to balance the sale of Romero with the retention of key players like van de Ven. As the transfer market continues to unfold, Spurs fans will be eagerly awaiting updates on the Romero situation, while also looking forward to the prospect of van de Ven committing his long-term future to the club.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mexico Supports Gianni Infantino Amid FIFA Governance Controversy
content:
Mexico's football federation has made a surprising move by publicly endorsing Fifa president Gianni Infantino, a decision that sets them apart from the rest of the Concacaf region. This development comes amidst growing tensions within the world football community, with Concacaf calling for a thorough review of Fifa's governance following the controversy surrounding the World Cup sell-off. The move by Mexico's football federation has sparked speculation that the country may be considering a switch to Conmebol, the South American football confederation.

This decision marks a significant break from the Concacaf's stance on the issue, which has been largely in line with Uefa's demands for meaningful change within Fifa. While Concacaf has yet to follow Uefa's lead in threatening to boycott tournaments if their objectives are not met, Mexico's move has added to the growing divisions within the football world. The implications of this decision are far-reaching, particularly given the potential for Mexico to re-evaluate its membership in Concacaf and potentially join Conmebol.

The move by Mexico's football federation has deepened the civil war within world football, with the country's decision to back Infantino likely to be met with both support and criticism from different quarters. As the situation continues to unfold, it remains to be seen how this development will impact the future of football in Mexico and beyond.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Atletico Madrid in Talks with Tottenham for Cristian Romero
content:
Atletico Madrid has begun exploratory talks with Tottenham Hotspur regarding a potential transfer of the club's captain, Cristian Romero. The Argentine defender is reportedly expected to leave North London this summer, sparking interest from various European clubs.

According to sources, Atletico Madrid is keen on securing Romero's services, given his impressive defensive skills and leadership qualities. The 28-year-old has been a key figure in Tottenham's backline, earning captaincy honors in the process. The outcome of these talks will be closely monitored, with fans and pundits alike eagerly awaiting news on the Argentine defender's next move.
author: BBC Sport

title: Sen. Mitch McConnell Discharged from Rehab Center
content:
Kentucky Sen. Mitch McConnell has made significant progress in his recovery, as he announced his discharge from a rehabilitation center on Thursday. The development comes more than 50 days after his initial hospitalization. McConnell, who has been a prominent figure in the US Senate for many years, had been undergoing treatment for an undisclosed medical condition. Despite the challenges he faced, the senator's discharge marks a positive milestone in his recovery journey.

According to reports, McConnell's hospitalization and subsequent rehabilitation were kept private, with the senator's office providing limited updates on his condition. However, his discharge statement suggests that he has made significant progress in his physical and possibly emotional recovery. As a key leader in the US Senate, McConnell's health and well-being are closely watched by the public and his colleagues. His return to full health is likely to be welcomed by those who rely on his experience and leadership.

The details surrounding McConnell's discharge and his future plans are not yet clear. However, his announcement is a positive development for the senator and those who have been following his recovery. As he returns home, McConnell can focus on regaining his strength and resuming his duties as a senator, where he will continue to play a crucial role in shaping the country's policies and laws.
author: NPR Politics

title: Colorado Jails Lag on Public Opioid Treatment Policies
content:
A recent study by researchers at the University of Colorado Anschutz has shed light on the ongoing challenges faced by Colorado's county jails in providing medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) treatment. Four years after the state passed a law mandating that county jails provide MOUD and make their policies publicly available, many facilities have failed to comply with this requirement. The study, which aimed to assess the availability of publicly disclosed policies for MOUD care in Colorado's county jails, revealed that a significant number of jails lack transparent and easily accessible information on their treatment protocols.

Researchers found that while some jails have made efforts to publish their policies, many others have not, leaving inmates and their families in the dark about the treatment options available to them. This lack of transparency can have serious consequences, as individuals struggling with opioid addiction may be unable to access the care they need to recover. Furthermore, the study highlights the ongoing need for Colorado's county jails to prioritize the implementation of evidence-based MOUD treatment programs and to provide clear, publicly accessible information about their policies and procedures.

The findings of this study underscore the importance of continued efforts to address the opioid epidemic and ensure that individuals in need of MOUD treatment receive the care they require. As policymakers and stakeholders work to address these challenges, the University of Colorado Anschutz researchers' study serves as a critical reminder of the need for transparency, accountability, and evidence-based practices in the delivery of MOUD treatment within Colorado's county jails.
author: Medical Xpress

title: U.S. corporations pay low federal taxes under 21% rate
content:
Large corporations frequently become the focus of public frustration when they appear to pay little or no federal income tax. The perception that these firms exploit loopholes or benefit from tax‑breaks fuels debate over the fairness of the U.S. tax system. Critics argue that the current structure allows some companies to minimize their tax liability to a fraction of what would be expected under a more progressive regime.

Since the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2018, the statutory federal corporate income tax rate has been set at 21 %. This rate is the lowest the United States has seen in decades, falling sharply from a historical peak of 53 % in 1969. The reduction was intended to stimulate investment and growth, but it has also contributed to concerns that large businesses can reduce their effective tax rates through deductions, credits, and other provisions built into the tax code.

The issue remains contentious as policymakers and the public weigh the benefits of a lower corporate tax rate against the revenue it generates for federal programs. While the 21 % rate has been in place for several years, the debate over corporate tax fairness continues to shape discussions about tax reform and economic equity.
author: Phys.org

title: Urban Growers Prioritize Access to Educational Resources for Pollinator-Friendly Farming
content:
Urban growers are increasingly adopting pollinator management practices to ensure the health and productivity of their crops. A recent study conducted by Michigan State University (MSU) entomologists Jen Roedel, Karma Thomas, and Zsofia Szendrei has shed light on the factors driving this trend. The researchers found that the decision to implement pollinator management practices is not influenced by the demographics of urban growers, such as age, income, or education level, but rather by their access to educational resources, labor, and other forms of farming support.

The study suggests that urban growers who have access to reliable sources of information, such as workshops, online tutorials, or extension services, are more likely to adopt pollinator management practices. Additionally, growers who have access to labor, either through hired help or family members, are also more likely to implement these practices. This is not surprising, given the importance of pollinators in maintaining crop yields and quality. However, the study also highlights the need for targeted support and education for urban growers, particularly those who may face barriers in accessing these resources.

The findings of this study have significant implications for policymakers and extension services seeking to support urban agriculture. By providing access to educational resources, labor, and other forms of support, these organizations can help urban growers to adopt pollinator management practices and improve the sustainability of their operations. As the demand for local, sustainable produce continues to grow, it is essential that urban growers have the tools and resources they need to succeed.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists Study Geoengineering Ice Arches to Preserve Arctic Sea Ice
content:
Scientists are exploring a novel approach to mitigate the effects of climate change on sea ice levels. Researchers from various institutions are conducting studies to determine whether artificially thickening ice blockages, known as ice shelves, between Canada and Greenland could prevent significant amounts of sea ice from flowing south to melt. This ice shelf, which spans over 1,000 kilometers, plays a crucial role in regulating the flow of ice from the Arctic into the North Atlantic.

The researchers are focusing on the Petermann Ice Shelf, a massive ice blockage located in the Canadian Arctic Archipelago. By artificially thickening this ice shelf, scientists hope to create a barrier that would slow down the flow of sea ice into the North Atlantic, where it would otherwise melt and contribute to rising sea levels. This approach is based on the understanding that ice shelves act as a brake on the flow of ice from the Arctic. By strengthening this natural barrier, researchers believe they can slow down the melting process and give the planet more time to adapt to the effects of climate change.

While the idea is still in its early stages, researchers note that artificially thickening the ice shelf would require significant resources and technological advancements. If successful, however, this approach could provide a new tool in the fight against climate change, allowing scientists to slow down the rate of sea ice melting and give the planet more time to adapt to the changing climate.
author: New Scientist

title: SpaceX Rocket Leaves Impact Crater on Moon
content:
SpaceX Rocket Leaves Lasting Impact on the Moon

In a dramatic display of celestial power, an out-of-control SpaceX rocket crashed into the moon earlier this week, leaving behind a lasting testament to its trajectory. The incident, which has garnered significant attention from astronomers and space enthusiasts alike, was confirmed by images captured by a Korean AeroSpace Administration (KASA) lunar orbiter. The satellite, which has been orbiting the moon, captured before-and-after photographs of the impact site, providing conclusive evidence of the rocket's collision with the lunar surface.

According to the images, the rocket's impact created a distinct crater on the moon's surface, marking a significant event in the ongoing exploration of our celestial neighbor. The incident serves as a poignant reminder of the risks and challenges associated with space travel and the importance of responsible mission planning. The KASA lunar orbiter's photographs offer a unique glimpse into the moon's geological makeup and the effects of external forces on its surface. As space agencies and private companies continue to push the boundaries of space exploration, incidents like this serve as a valuable learning experience for the industry.

The aftermath of the SpaceX rocket's crash is a significant development in the ongoing quest for space knowledge and exploration. As the space community continues to grapple with the implications of this event, the images captured by the KASA lunar orbiter will undoubtedly provide valuable insights into the moon's composition and the effects of external forces on its surface.
author: New Scientist

title: US Reaches $1.2B Deal with German Firm to Halt Offshore Wind Projects
content:
**Scientists Discover New Species of Ancient Human in the Philippines**

In a groundbreaking discovery, a team of international scientists has unearthed a previously unknown species of ancient human in the Philippines. The findings, published in a recent study, have shed new light on the evolution of human species in the region. According to researchers, the newly discovered species, named Homo luzonensis, is believed to have lived on the island of Luzon at least 50,000 years ago.

The discovery was made in Callao Cave, a limestone cave system in Cagayan Valley, where archaeologists found a trove of fossilized remains, including teeth, bones, and stone tools. The fossils, which date back to the Late Pleistocene era, suggest that Homo luzonensis was a small, agile species, with adults standing at around 4 feet tall. The team believes that this species may have lived in isolation from other human populations, leading to the development of unique physical characteristics.

The discovery of Homo luzonensis has significant implications for our understanding of human evolution and the history of human migration in the region. The study's lead author, Dr. Florent Detroit, noted that the findings provide "new insights into the complexity of human evolution" and highlight the importance of continued research into the region's rich archaeological heritage. The discovery is set to spark further debate and research into the origins of human species in the Philippines and beyond.
author: Hacker News

title: The Manosphere Exploits Young Men with Multibillion-Dollar Industry
content:
A recent study has shed light on the darker side of social media influence, highlighting the exploitation of young men who are being sold false promises of success and fame. According to the report, many of these individuals are being targeted by online influencers who claim to offer shortcuts to achieving social status, wealth, and recognition. These influencers often peddle classes, pills, and other products that promise to boost their followers' online presence, but in reality, deliver little to no results.

The report reveals that these young men are often lured into purchasing expensive courses, supplements, and other products that claim to guarantee success. However, the report found that these products are often nothing more than scams, designed to part young men from their money. Furthermore, the report highlights the psychological toll of this exploitation, with many young men feeling resentful, anxious, and depressed as they struggle to achieve the online success they were promised. The report's findings suggest that this is a widespread problem, with thousands of young men being targeted by these unscrupulous influencers every year.

The report's authors are calling for greater regulation of the social media industry, as well as increased awareness among young people about the dangers of online exploitation. They argue that it is essential to educate young men about the risks of being targeted by influencers, and to provide them with the skills and resources they need to succeed online in a healthy and sustainable way. By taking these steps, we can help to prevent the exploitation of young men and promote a more positive and responsible online culture.

title: Smart Glasses Comparison 2026
content:
Breakthrough in Wearable Technology: Smart Contact Lenses Debut

In a groundbreaking innovation, researchers have unveiled smart contact lenses that enable users to interact with artificial intelligence assistants, enjoy music, and access display screens directly from the comfort of their own eyes. This cutting-edge wearable technology has been touted as a potential game-changer in the realm of personal computing and communication.

The smart contact lenses, developed by a team of experts in the field, feature a tiny microchip and a miniature display screen embedded within the lens itself. Users can communicate with AI assistants, receive notifications, and access various apps, all without the need for a separate device. The lenses also come equipped with a built-in speaker, allowing users to listen to music or receive audio cues. According to the developers, the lenses are designed to be comfortable and safe for extended wear, with a focus on seamless integration with the user's daily life.

As the smart contact lenses enter the market, experts predict a significant shift in the way people interact with technology. With this innovative wearable, users will be able to access a wealth of information and services directly from their eyes, revolutionizing the way we live, work, and communicate. While the technology is still in its early stages, it has the potential to transform the world of wearable technology and beyond.

title: Affordable Gaming Laptops Compared: Lenovo, MSI, Alienware Options
content:
The cost of gaming laptops has been steadily increasing, making it challenging for consumers to find affordable options that meet their performance needs. As a result, many are forced to compromise on either price or quality, often ending up with a laptop that fails to deliver a satisfactory gaming experience. However, there are still some options available that strike a balance between performance and cost, providing a viable solution for those on a budget.

For those looking for a gaming laptop that won't break the bank, several models stand out from the rest. These laptops offer a combination of capable processors, sufficient RAM, and dedicated graphics cards, allowing for smooth gameplay and decent frame rates. While they may not boast the latest and greatest hardware, they are often priced significantly lower than their high-end counterparts, making them an attractive option for budget-conscious gamers. Additionally, some manufacturers are now offering more affordable lines of gaming laptops, which can provide a more accessible entry point for those new to PC gaming.

In conclusion, while the rising cost of gaming laptops can be a barrier for many, there are still affordable options available that can provide a good gaming experience. By considering factors such as performance, cost, and brand reputation, consumers can find a laptop that meets their needs without exceeding their budget. As the gaming laptop market continues to evolve, it's likely that more affordable options will become available, making it easier for gamers to find a laptop that delivers the performance they need at a price they can afford.
author: Wired

title: One Night Only' Explores Sex Dystopia in Modern New York
content:
New York City, known for its vibrant energy and diverse culture, has been transformed into a surreal landscape in the upcoming film "One Night Only." The movie's trailer showcases a seemingly ordinary modern metropolis, but with a twist: a law has been enacted that restricts single individuals to having sex only one night a year. While some might expect a traditional romantic comedy, the film instead delves into the complexities of this unusual premise.

The movie takes an episodic approach to explore the lives of its characters, particularly two special individuals, Monica Barbaro and Callum Turner, who find themselves navigating this peculiar reality. Rather than focusing on the societal implications or the moral consequences of such a law, "One Night Only" prioritizes the intimate and often humorous aspects of human relationships. The film raises thought-provoking questions about the nature of desire, attraction, and intimacy, all set against the backdrop of a society where sex has become a rare and highly anticipated event.

As the film's unique premise suggests, "One Night Only" promises to be a captivating and unconventional exploration of human connection in a world where sex has become a luxury. With its blend of humor, drama, and intrigue, the movie is sure to spark interesting conversations and leave audiences pondering the themes and questions it raises.
author: The Verge

title: Abelardo de la Espriella Becomes Colombian President
content:
Colombia is set to usher in a new era as President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella takes office on August 8. The former lawyer won a narrow victory in June's run-off election, securing the presidency by less than a percentage point. De la Espriella's campaign promises have sparked significant attention, particularly his vow to launch a comprehensive war on drug gangs and strengthen ties with the United States. This shift in policy direction is expected to have far-reaching implications for Colombia's domestic and foreign policy landscape.

As a right-wing populist, de la Espriella's leadership style is being compared to that of El Salvador's Nayib Bukele and Argentina's Javier Milei. His unorthodox approach to governance is also evident in the unusual location chosen for his swearing-in ceremony. The details surrounding this event have not been made public, adding to the intrigue surrounding de la Espriella's ascension to the presidency. As he prepares to take office, Colombians are eagerly awaiting the implementation of his campaign promises, which are expected to have a significant impact on the country's future.

De la Espriella's presidency is poised to mark a significant turning point in Colombia's history, with the country's relations with the United States likely to be a key area of focus. The new president's commitment to tackling the country's long-standing issue of drug-related violence will also be closely watched. As de la Espriella begins his tenure, he will face numerous challenges, but his determination to drive change has already generated considerable interest and anticipation among Colombians and international observers alike.
author: France 24

title: French Farmers Face Climate Crisis Impacts
content:
Climate Disruption Hits French Agriculture Hard

As the 2026 growing season draws to a close, farmers in southwestern France are facing the harsh realities of climate disruption. Jean-Mathieu Thévenot, a farmer in the French Basque Country and member of the Confédération Paysanne farmers' union, has witnessed firsthand the devastating impact of changing weather patterns on local agriculture. According to Thévenot, the current year marks a turning point where climate disruption has become an immediate concern for farmers, affecting not only their livelihoods but also the region's economy and culture.

Thévenot's own farm has been partially spared from the worst of the disruption, as their production cycle ended earlier in the season. However, he has been observing the struggles of vegetable growers, livestock farmers, and fruit producers who are struggling to adapt to the changing climate. The situation is particularly dire for those whose production cycles are still ongoing, with many facing crop failures, reduced yields, and significant economic losses. As the effects of climate disruption become more pronounced, Thévenot and his fellow farmers are working tirelessly to find ways to mitigate the damage and ensure the long-term sustainability of their farms.

The challenges faced by French farmers are not unique, but rather part of a broader global trend. As a member of the international movement La Via Campesina, Thévenot is part of a global network of farmers working together to address the impacts of climate disruption and promote sustainable agricultural practices. As the situation continues to unfold, it remains to be seen how farmers in southwestern France and beyond will adapt to the changing climate and ensure the long-term viability of their farms.
author: France 24

title: Danube Drought Exposes WWII Ships and Mammoth Remains
content:
Drought and extreme heat have brought severe consequences to Europe's waterways, with the Danube River experiencing record-low water levels. The Danube, the second longest river in Europe, has seen its water levels drop significantly, exposing long-buried secrets. In Germany, the remains of dozens of German warships from World War II have begun to emerge from the water, offering a glimpse into the country's past. The hulls of these vessels, which have been submerged for decades, are now visible, serving as a poignant reminder of the region's complex history.

The drought's impact extends beyond the Danube, with other European rivers also feeling the effects. In Germany, fishing boats have been stuck near the banks of the Rhine, a major commercial waterway, as the reduced water levels have left them unable to navigate. Meanwhile, in France, sections of the Loire riverbed are partially dry, a stark contrast to the river's usual flow. The situation is particularly concerning in Romania, where the remains of an ancient mammoth were recently uncovered due to the low water levels. This discovery offers a unique insight into the region's prehistoric past and highlights the significance of the Danube's role in shaping the country's history.

As the drought continues to grip Europe, concerns are growing about the long-term impact on the region's ecosystems and waterways. The low water levels are not only affecting the navigation of rivers but also posing a threat to the region's biodiversity. As authorities work to address the crisis, the exposed remnants of the past serve as a poignant reminder of the importance of preserving these natural resources for future generations.
author: France 24

title: Houthi strikes increase as Saudi Arabia prepares for attacks amid rising tensions
content:
The recent escalation of hostilities between the United States and Israel over Iranian activities has coincided with a sharp rise in tensions between Yemen’s Houthi movement and Saudi Arabia. Since the two countries intensified their military cooperation against Iran, the Houthis have increased missile and drone attacks on Saudi shipping lanes and oil infrastructure, citing the broader regional conflict as a catalyst for their actions.

Saudi Arabia has responded with a series of airstrikes targeting Houthi positions in Yemen, claiming to neutralize threats to its maritime routes and to deter further aggression. The Saudi-led coalition has also intensified naval patrols in the Red Sea, while the United Arab Emirates has stepped up its own defensive measures. The United States, which has maintained a presence in the region, has issued statements urging restraint but has not directly intervened in the Houthi‑Saudi dispute.

The convergence of these conflicts raises concerns about a potential spill‑over into the wider Gulf region. Analysts warn that continued Houthi attacks could disrupt global oil supplies, while Saudi retaliation risks drawing the country into a broader confrontation. Diplomatic efforts are underway to deescalate the situation, but the intertwined nature of the US‑Israel‑Iran triangle and the Yemen conflict suggests that further tensions are likely unless a comprehensive resolution is achieved.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump Faces Escalation Trap with Iran, Says Professor Pape
content:
University of Chicago political science professor Robert Pape has warned that President Donald Trump’s approach to Iran could lock the United States into an “escalation trap.”  Pape, who has long studied the dynamics of conflict, argues that Trump’s hard‑line rhetoric and willingness to confront Tehran—through sanctions, military posturing and the threat of force—have provoked a reciprocal response that raises the stakes for both sides.  The professor points to a series of incidents, from the 2020 U.S. drone strike that killed Iranian General Qasem Soleimani to the subsequent Iranian missile attacks on U.S. forces in Iraq, as evidence that each action triggers a counter‑action, creating a cycle that is difficult to break.

In his analysis, Pape stresses that escalation is not inevitable but becomes highly probable when leaders ignore diplomatic channels and rely on coercive measures.  He notes that Trump’s administration has repeatedly dismissed or weakened multilateral agreements, such as the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, while simultaneously demanding concessions from Iran that the Iranian leadership has deemed unacceptable.  This combination of punitive measures and diplomatic isolation, according to Pape, pushes Iran toward more aggressive posturing, thereby tightening the escalation trap and limiting the U.S.’s strategic options.

The professor’s assessment underscores the risks of a confrontational strategy that escalates tensions without a clear exit plan.  While the U.S. remains a key player in Middle Eastern security, Pape’s warning suggests that a more measured, multilateral approach may be necessary to avoid a spiral of violence that could destabilize the region further.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Houthis expand cross‑border attacks, raising risk of major battle in Yemen
content:
The Houthi movement in Yemen has intensified its cross‑border operations, targeting sites in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, prompting analysts to warn that a more lethal phase of the regional conflict could be looming. In the past month the rebels have launched missile and drone strikes on Saudi oil facilities, a military airport in the Eastern Province, and a UAE‑operated port in the Red Sea, expanding the geographic scope of their campaign beyond the Yemeni theater.

Security experts say the broadened strike pattern reflects the Houthis’ growing logistical capacity and a strategic aim to pressure coalition partners supporting the Yemeni government. The escalation follows a series of maritime attacks on commercial vessels transiting the Red Sea, which have already disrupted international shipping lanes. Regional diplomats have called for renewed cease‑fire talks, but officials caution that the heightened offensive posture may trigger a cycle of retaliation, raising the risk of a bloodier war in the coming weeks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Tehran discusses bill to bar US and Israeli vessels from Strait of Hormuz
content:
Tehran is reportedly preparing legislation that would prohibit United States and Israeli-registered vessels from transiting the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway that channels roughly a fifth of global oil shipments. The draft bill, discussed in recent sessions of Iran’s parliament, calls for the designation of any ship bearing U.S. or Israeli flags as “hostile” and mandates that they be denied passage through the strategic chokepoint that lies between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

If enacted, the measure could disrupt international shipping routes and heighten tensions in an already volatile region, where Iran has previously threatened to close the strait in response to sanctions or perceived aggression. Analysts note that the proposal follows a series of diplomatic confrontations involving Iranian nuclear negotiations and recent incidents involving naval vessels in the area. The bill’s progress will be monitored by regional governments and maritime authorities, as any restriction on navigation could have significant economic and security ramifications for global energy markets.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Tottenham Captain Cristian Romero Linked to Potential Transfer to Arsenal
content:
Rumors Surround Cristian Romero Amid Transfer Speculation

Reports are emerging that Tottenham Hotspur's captain, Cristian Romero, has caught the attention of Arsenal, sparking speculation about a potential transfer drama. According to The Athletic, the Gunners are interested in securing the Argentine defender's services, but it remains uncertain whether Spurs will be willing to let him leave. The transfer window is shaping up to be an exciting and unpredictable one, with several high-profile players caught in the midst of transfer speculation. title: US Companies Receive Tariff Refunds
content:
Tariff Refunds Boost Corporate Earnings on Wall Street

In a significant development, many major companies on Wall Street are reporting a substantial boost in earnings due to the recent tariff refunds handed out by the US government. The latest quarter has seen the Trump administration refunding the bulk of the $100 billion returned so far, providing a welcome windfall for several corporations. This move is expected to have a positive impact on the companies' bottom lines as they release their quarterly earnings reports.

Amazon is among the beneficiaries, with the e-commerce giant receiving a tariff refund of $600 million. Apple also reported a significant gain, with the refund adding $0.11 in diluted earnings per share for the quarter. Similarly, PepsiCo informed investors that the company had received a substantial refund, although the exact amount was not disclosed. These refunds are a result of the Trump administration's decision to waive or refund tariffs imposed on imported goods, providing relief to companies that had been bearing the costs of these duties.

As the companies continue to report their earnings, the impact of the tariff refunds is becoming increasingly evident. The refunds are expected to provide a much-needed boost to the companies' financial performance, helping to offset the costs associated with the tariffs. With many major corporations set to release their earnings reports in the coming weeks, investors will be closely watching to see the extent to which the tariff refunds have contributed to their financial performance.
author: The Hill

title: Earth's Core Magnetic Field Reverses Direction Suddenly
content:
Scientists have detected an unexpected reversal in the flow of Earth’s molten iron core beneath the Pacific Ocean, marking a significant shift in the planetary mechanism responsible for generating the geomagnetic field. The discovery, derived from recent satellite observations, highlights a sudden change in deep-Earth fluid dynamics that have historically been difficult to track in real time.

Satellite measurements indicate that the high-speed jet of liquid iron, which had maintained a consistent eastward trajectory for decades, abruptly shifted direction before beginning to decelerate. Researchers note that the ongoing weakening of the surge suggests the event may represent a transient phase within a broader, poorly understood natural cycle rather than a permanent structural change. The data offer valuable insight into the outer core’s convection patterns, which drive the geodynamo process that sustains the magnetic shield protecting the surface from solar and cosmic radiation.

While the core reversal has no direct impact on surface environments or human technology, the observation reinforces the highly dynamic nature of Earth’s interior. Sustained satellite monitoring and advanced geophysical modeling will be necessary to determine whether this directional shift follows a predictable cyclical pattern or constitutes an isolated fluctuation in the planet’s magnetic evolution.
author: Science Daily

title: Plastic-Free Coffee Makers Gain Popularity
content:
Rising concerns over microplastic contamination in everyday consumables have brought household coffee brewing equipment under scrutiny, prompting manufacturers to develop a new generation of plastic-free drip coffee makers. Recent studies indicate that conventional plastic brewers can shed microscopic particles into hot water during the brewing process, introducing synthetic contaminants into daily coffee consumption. In response, several companies have introduced alternative designs constructed entirely from glass, stainless steel, and ceramic materials, aiming to eliminate plastic contact with hot liquids while maintaining standard brewing performance.

The presence of microplastics in coffee has been linked to the thermal degradation of polymer components when exposed to high temperatures and acidic coffee grounds. Traditional drip machines often rely on plastic reservoirs, tubing, and showerheads, which can release particles ranging from one to five micrometers in size during each brew cycle. The emerging plastic-free models replace these components with heat-resistant, non-porous materials that withstand brewing temperatures without chemical leaching. Industry analysts note that consumer awareness of environmental and health implications has accelerated demand for these alternatives, with several major kitchen appliance brands now integrating plastic-free options into their product lines.

As regulatory agencies and
author: Wired

title: South Africa Textile Industry Faces Workforce Crisis
content:
South Africa’s textile sector is confronting a sudden workforce shortage as thousands of migrant workers have fled the country following violent xenophobic protests. The unrest, sparked by an anti‑immigrant campaign led by the group March and March, was aimed at freeing up jobs for South Africans, a demographic in which one‑third of the population remains unemployed.  

Factory owners in Newcastle, a key hub for textile production, report that many positions remain unfilled. “We have not yet been able to replace the workers who left,” said a spokesperson for a local textile firm. The exodus has left production lines stalled and supply chains disrupted, raising concerns about the industry’s ability to meet domestic and export demand.  

Industry analysts warn that the crisis could deepen if the current shortage persists, potentially prompting firms to seek alternative sourcing strategies or invest in automation. Meanwhile, government officials are monitoring the situation closely, urging a balanced approach that addresses both employment pressures and the need for social cohesion.
author: France 24

title: Nigerian Artist Turns Clay into Paint for Portraits
content:
In Lagos, Nigerian artist Emmanuel Olatunde is redefining portraiture by turning the very soil that surrounds his studio into pigment. The 39‑year‑old has devised a process that extracts natural clay from the earth beneath his feet, refines it, and transforms it into a paint that he uses to render human likenesses. His method blends scientific precision with artistic intuition, allowing the earthy tones of the clay to lend depth and authenticity to his canvases.

Olatunde’s background in chemistry informs every stage of his technique. He first tests the mineral composition of local clays, then subjects them to a series of washes and sieves to isolate the fine particles that will become pigment. The resulting paint retains the clay’s natural hue while gaining the consistency required for fine brushwork. By sourcing his materials locally, he also emphasizes sustainability, reducing the need for imported pigments and highlighting the cultural heritage of Lagos’s geology.

The artist’s work has attracted attention from galleries and collectors interested in eco‑conscious art practices. Olatunde’s portraits, characterized by subtle earth tones and a tactile quality, have been displayed in several Lagos exhibitions and are slated for a touring show across West Africa. His pioneering approach demonstrates how scientific knowledge can expand the possibilities of traditional media, offering a fresh perspective on the relationship between environment and artistic expression.
author: France 24

title: Thailand School Shooting Leaves Eight Dead, 15 Injured
content:
A shooting at a Thai school has left at least eight people dead and 15 others wounded, authorities said on Tuesday.  The incident occurred inside the premises of a secondary school in the central province of Nakhon Pathom, according to police reports.  The gunman, a 17‑year‑old student, was apprehended by security staff before he could leave the building.

Investigators say the suspect fired a number of shots from a handgun that he had brought onto campus.  The school was closed for the remainder of the day and emergency services responded immediately, treating the injured at the nearest hospital.  The Ministry of Education has announced an investigation into the incident and is reviewing security protocols at schools nationwide.

The Thai police are conducting a full inquiry into the motive behind the attack and are cooperating with the Ministry of Interior to ensure the safety of students.  The school’s administration has pledged to provide support to victims and families while the investigation continues.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UK and France avoid Iran confrontation as US pushes Hormuz naval mission
content:
London and Paris have signaled that they do not intend to provoke Iran as the United States and Israel become embroiled in a widening regional conflict, analysts said on Tuesday. Both governments have emphasized diplomatic engagement over military escalation, and European leaders have broadly rejected any steps that could draw the continent into a direct confrontation with Tehran. The stance follows a series of public remarks by the UK foreign secretary and the French president, who warned that escalation would jeopardise European security and economic interests, while Iran has issued increasingly hostile statements in response to Israeli operations.

Analysts note that the consensus across the European Union reflects a desire to contain the hostilities and prevent the war from expanding beyond the immediate US‑Israeli theater. EU foreign ministers have reiterated support for a negotiated resolution and have called on Iran to refrain from retaliatory actions that could trigger a broader clash. By maintaining a low‑key diplomatic approach, the UK, France and their European partners aim to limit the risk of a direct Europe‑Iran confrontation while monitoring developments closely.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Saudi Pro League striker Ivan Toney charged with assault in UK
content:
Ivan Toney, the Tottenham Hotspur striker, has been formally charged with assault in connection with an incident that allegedly occurred on 6 December of last year in the United Kingdom. The charge, announced by the Crown Prosecution Service, stems from a police investigation that concluded sufficient evidence existed to proceed with criminal proceedings against the 30‑year‑old footballer.

The case will be heard in a magistrates’ court, where Toney will enter a plea and await a trial date. If convicted, he could face a fine, a community‑service order or a short custodial sentence, depending on the severity of the offence as determined by the court. The charge adds to a series of legal challenges the player has faced in recent months, and the outcome may affect his availability for club and international duties pending the resolution of the matter.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Central Europe records extreme heat as Italy issues highest alert for major cities
content:
A severe heatwave sweeping Central Europe has pushed temperatures to unprecedented levels, with Slovakia and Austria both recording their highest readings of the year. In Bratislava, the mercury climbed to 38.5 °C, eclipsing the previous summer record, while Vienna saw temperatures reach 39.2 °C, the hottest day since reliable measurements began in the 1950s. Meteorological services in both countries attribute the extreme values to a persistent high‑pressure system that has stalled over the region, drawing hot air from the Mediterranean and limiting cloud cover.

In response to the escalating conditions, Italy’s civil protection agency placed all 27 of the nation’s major cities under the highest heat alert, the first nationwide issuance of its kind. Authorities have activated emergency cooling centers, issued health advisories urging residents to stay hydrated and avoid outdoor activity during peak hours, and mobilized additional resources for vulnerable populations. Forecast models indicate the heatwave could persist for several more days, prompting neighboring countries to monitor the situation closely and prepare for possible further temperature spikes.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Norway's Football Federation Calls for Infantino's Resignation
content:
Fifa President Gianni Infantino Faces Call to Resign Amid Controversy

In a significant development, the Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) has requested Fifa President Gianni Infantino to resign with immediate effect, citing his failed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors as the final nail in the coffin for his presidency. This move marks the first time a national federation has directly called for Infantino's resignation, underscoring the growing discontent with his leadership. The decision was made during a meeting of the NFF on Thursday night, following a series of controversies that have plagued Fifa in recent times.

Norway has long been at the forefront of efforts to scrutinize Fifa's governance, and the latest crisis surrounding Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme has pushed the federation's faith in his leadership beyond repair. The scheme, which aimed to sell stakes in the World Cup, has been widely criticized for its potential to compromise the integrity of the tournament. With Norway's call to action, the pressure on Infantino to step down is mounting, and it remains to be seen whether he will heed the call or continue to battle for support around the world.

The NFF's decision to request Infantino's resignation marks a significant escalation in the crisis surrounding his presidency, and it is likely to have far-reaching implications for Fifa's governance and leadership. As the situation continues to unfold, one thing is clear: the future of Gianni Infantino's presidency hangs in the balance, and the outcome is far from certain.
author: Guardian Sport

title: 2027 Memory Capacity Sold Out
content:
Ramageddon, the ongoing global shortage of computer memory, has reportedly extended into 2027, with many manufacturers reporting that all available memory capacity for the year has already been sold out. According to a report from Ign.com, the persistent supply chain disruptions that began in 2023 have continued to constrain the production of DRAM and NAND flash, leaving hardware developers and data‑center operators scrambling for inventory. The article notes that the shortage has already impacted the rollout of new servers, gaming consoles, and high‑performance computing platforms.

The report details that major memory suppliers have announced that their 2027 production lines are fully booked, citing a combination of high demand from the consumer electronics sector, increased cloud‑computing workloads, and lingering logistical bottlenecks. While some analysts suggest that the situation may improve later in the year as new manufacturing capacity comes online, the current snapshot indicates that the memory market remains tight. The piece was shared on the Hacker News community, where it has garnered 35 points and 11 comments, reflecting significant interest from industry professionals and technologists.

In summary, the 2027 memory capacity sell‑out underscores the continued volatility of the semiconductor supply chain. As the industry adapts to these constraints, stakeholders are monitoring potential shifts in pricing, inventory strategies, and the pace of new chip production. The situation remains fluid, and further updates are expected as manufacturers announce any changes to their production schedules.
author: Hacker News

title: Meta Ordered to Pay $567M in New Mexico Child Safety Case
content:
Meta has been ordered to pay $567 million in the second phase of New Mexico’s landmark child‑safety lawsuit, bringing the total amount the company faces to nearly $1 billion. The Santa Fe district court, in a ruling released Thursday, found that Meta’s platforms are a “significant contributing cause” of a statewide teen mental‑health crisis that the court said affects public health and safety across the state. The case, which has been described as a “public nuisance” action, seeks to hold the social‑media giant accountable for practices that the court determined endanger young people.

The judge’s decision follows years of litigation in which the state’s attorney general has argued that Meta’s algorithms and content moderation policies create an environment that exploits and harms adolescents. In a statement accompanying the ruling, the attorney general emphasized that the case “has always been about protecting children, standing up for families, and making sure that one of the world’s largest technology companies cannot profit from practices that endanger young people without consequence.” The $567 million award represents the second tranche of damages, with earlier phases already imposing substantial financial penalties and requiring the company to implement stricter safeguards.

This ruling marks a significant moment in the broader debate over technology companies’ responsibilities to minors. By labeling Meta a public nuisance and mandating a near‑billion‑dollar payment, the court sets a precedent that could influence future regulatory actions and corporate policies nationwide. The decision also signals a growing willingness among state courts to hold large platforms directly accountable for the social and psychological impacts of their services on vulnerable populations.
author: The Verge

title: Trump Imposes 15% Tariff on Polysilicon Imports
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump has announced a new 15 % tariff on imported goods made with polysilicon, a key raw material used in microchip and solar‑panel production. The measure, scheduled to take effect on 4 December, targets products that are predominantly sourced from China, the world’s largest polysilicon producer. The tariff is intended to strengthen domestic supply chains for critical technologies that underpin the United States’ competitiveness in artificial intelligence and renewable energy.

Polysilicon is essential for the fabrication of integrated circuits and photovoltaic cells, and its concentration in China has raised concerns about supply‑chain vulnerability. By imposing the tariff, the administration seeks to encourage domestic manufacturing of this material and reduce reliance on foreign sources. The policy aligns with broader U.S. efforts to secure strategic components against geopolitical risks and to support the growth of the domestic chip and solar‑panel industries.

The move is part of a broader strategy to counter China’s technological ascendancy. By tightening import restrictions on polysilicon, the U.S. aims to protect its semiconductor and clean‑energy sectors, ensuring that American companies can compete effectively in high‑tech markets while safeguarding national security interests.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Sri Lanka Deploys Troops to Quell Prison Overcrowding Unrest
content:
Officials in Sri Lanka have linked the country’s escalating prison unrest to acute overcrowding, noting that the nation’s correctional facilities are operating at roughly four times their intended capacity. The surge in inmate numbers has strained resources, heightened tensions, and increased the likelihood of conflict among prisoners.

The overcrowded conditions have been cited by authorities as a primary driver of recent disturbances, including riots and protests within several major jails. With limited space, inadequate sanitation, and restricted access to basic services, inmates have expressed frustration, leading to heightened security challenges for prison staff.

In response, the government has announced plans to expand capacity and improve management of the prison system, aiming to reduce overcrowding and mitigate further unrest. The measures are expected to address the root causes of the current tensions and restore stability within Sri Lanka’s correctional facilities.
author: Euronews

title: Heatwaves Prompt Early Bordeaux Wine Harvest
content:
French winegrowers in the Bordeaux region began harvesting their grapes on Thursday, a day that historically falls after the summer break. The early start follows a season of consecutive heatwaves, drought and widespread wildfires that have pushed the harvest window forward. “Usually, we’d still be on vacation,” one grape-picker told the newspaper Sud Ouest, underscoring how the timing of the work has shifted.

Despite the environmental challenges, winemakers insist that the quality of the wine will not be compromised. The earlier harvest has become a growing trend across France as climate change forces farmers to adapt, with some switching to less water‑intensive crops. The shift to an earlier picking schedule is part of a broader effort to maintain production levels while responding to the increasingly unpredictable weather patterns that have marked recent summers.

The Bordeaux harvest, a key indicator of the country’s viticultural health, illustrates how climate change is reshaping agricultural calendars. While the early start may raise logistical concerns, the industry’s confidence in maintaining wine quality remains high, and the adaptation measures taken by growers suggest a proactive approach to the evolving climate realities.
author: France 24

title: Thousands protest Argentina private property bill outside Senate
content:
Thousands of demonstrators gathered outside Argentina’s Senate on Thursday to protest a controversial private‑property bill, turning the assembly into a scene of clashes that required the use of tear gas and rubber‑bullet fire. Protesters, many of whom carried signs denouncing the legislation, confronted police as the demonstration escalated into scuffles, prompting authorities to intervene with crowd‑control measures. The unrest highlighted deep public opposition to provisions perceived as threatening national control over land resources.

In response to the outcry, President Javier Milei’s administration removed the bill’s most contentious clause, which would have lifted limits on foreign ownership of Argentine land. Despite the amendment, the removal has not quelled the anger, and the protests continued to underscore broader concerns about the government’s approach to private property rights and economic reform. The episode reflects ongoing tension between Milei’s reform agenda and segments of the population wary of foreign investment in the country’s agricultural sector. Peter O’Brien has more.
author: France 24

title: FIFA governance crisis intensifies after Forward Entity proposal collapse
content:
Alison Sargent announced the arrival of International Sports Journalist Thando Sibiya, who will examine the ongoing FIFA governance crisis. Sibiya contends that the dispute over the abandoned FIFA Forward Entity proposal—a plan to sell a permanent stake in FIFA’s commercial rights—should be viewed not as an isolated commercial failure but as a catalyst that revealed deeper institutional tensions that have accumulated during Gianni Infantino’s presidency.

In his analysis, Sibiya links the stalled commercial deal to a series of related developments, including the resignation of a senior adviser, UEFA’s increasingly confrontational posture, disagreements over referee protection policies, and competing interests between UEFA and the Confederation of African Football. These elements, he argues, underscore a broader contest over governance, legitimacy, commercialisation, and geopolitical influence within world football, highlighting a fundamental struggle over who will shape the sport’s future.
author: France 24

title: Belgium confronts legacy of 1894 Antwerp human zoo exhibition
content:
Antwerp’s 1894 World’s Fair featured a controversial exhibit known as the Congo Pavilion, where 144 Congolese individuals were forcibly transported to Belgium and displayed for European visitors. Marketed as a “human zoo,” the pavilion presented the men, women and children in a staged environment meant to illustrate colonial “progress,” while the participants were subjected to confinement, inadequate sanitation and limited medical care. Within the duration of the fair, seven of the men succumbed to disease, underscoring the lethal conditions they endured.

The episode has resurfaced in recent years as a focal point of Belgium’s reckoning with its colonial past, prompting historians, cultural institutions and public officials to acknowledge the event as one of the nation’s darkest chapters. Exhibitions, academic research and parliamentary discussions have highlighted the forced nature of the display and its lasting impact on collective memory, reinforcing calls for broader education about Belgium’s role in the Congo and the human cost of its imperial ambitions.
author: France 24

title: Professionals Seek Islamic Scholarship at Darul Qasim in Chicago
content:
Chicago’s Darul Qasim Institute has seen a notable increase in enrollment from professionals such as physicians, attorneys, and engineers seeking advanced study of Islamic jurisprudence and theology. According to the institute’s enrollment records, the number of adult learners holding graduate or professional degrees rose from 112 in 2022 to 287 in 2025, reflecting a broader trend of highly educated individuals pursuing structured religious education alongside their careers.

The institute attributes the growth to several programmatic adjustments designed for busy schedules, including weekend seminars, evening lectures, and a suite of online courses covering topics from classical fiqh to contemporary bioethical issues. Faculty members, many of whom hold Ph.D. degrees from Western universities, have emphasized the relevance of Islamic scholarship to modern professional challenges, offering case studies that integrate legal ethics, medical decision‑making, and corporate governance with traditional sources. Partnerships with local hospitals and law firms have also facilitated workshops where participants apply scholarly insights to real‑world scenarios, further reinforcing the practical appeal of the curriculum.

Institutional leaders project continued expansion as demand for interdisciplinary religious education persists. Plans announced at a recent board meeting include the launch of a certificate program in Islamic Ethics for Professionals and the addition of a dedicated research library. Darul Qasim’s leadership expects these initiatives to sustain the upward enrollment trajectory and to solidify the institute’s role as a hub for scholarly engagement among Chicago’s professional community.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Youth-led job and recruitment protests spread in Jharkhand
content:
Weeks after the CJP protests that disrupted Delhi’s streets, a new youth‑led movement is gaining momentum in Jharkhand, focusing on employment opportunities and the transparency of recruitment processes. Organisers, primarily students and recent graduates, say the state’s job market has failed to absorb the growing number of job‑seekers, prompting them to stage rallies, circulate petitions and use social media to highlight alleged irregularities in government hiring practices. The movement’s leaders have called for an independent audit of recruitment procedures, faster implementation of skill‑development schemes, and the creation of a dedicated portal for vacancy announcements.

State officials have acknowledged the concerns, noting that Jharkhand’s unemployment rate remains above the national average and that recent efforts to streamline hiring are underway. The department of labour has pledged to review the grievances and to convene a round‑table with youth representatives within the next month. As the movement gathers further support across districts, observers note that its emergence reflects a broader pattern of youth activism in India, where localized campaigns are following the high‑profile CJP protests in the capital.
author: BBC World

title: Sports quiz of the week: big deals, bad luck, nicknames and hidden talents
content:
Global Sports Scene Heats Up with Multiple Championships

In a thrilling display of athletic prowess, several high-profile championships have taken place across various sports disciplines. The football world witnessed a nail-biting conclusion to the UEFA Champions League, with Real Madrid emerging victorious against Liverpool in the final. Meanwhile, darts fans were treated to an electrifying performance by Gerwyn Price, who secured the PDC World Darts Championship title.

In the world of cycling, the Tour de France witnessed an exciting finish, with Jonas Vingegaard claiming the overall victory. On the ice, the curling community was abuzz with the conclusion of the Scottish Curling Championships, where the Rindone rink took home the top prize. The athletics world also saw some impressive performances, with Noah Lyles setting a new world record in the 200m dash at the Diamond League meeting. Golf enthusiasts were on the edge of their seats as Rory McIlroy triumphed at the Open Championship, securing his fifth major title.

As the sports world continues to evolve, fans are eagerly anticipating the next major championships. With multiple disciplines pushing the boundaries of human performance, it's clear that this year will be remembered as a remarkable one for sports enthusiasts worldwide.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Sturgeon Criticized by Ex-Colleagues Over SNP Election Campaign
content:
Former First Minister Nicola Sturgeon's recent comments criticizing the SNP's 2026 election campaign have sparked an intense backlash from her former colleagues within the party. Sturgeon, who served as the leader of the Scottish National Party (SNP) from 2014 to 2023, made the remarks in a private meeting, which were later leaked to the press. According to sources, Sturgeon expressed concerns about the party's strategy and messaging, suggesting that it may not be effective in securing a strong presence in the upcoming elections.

The comments have been met with a stern response from several ex-colleagues, who have defended the party's current leadership and election campaign. Former SNP MSPs have taken to social media to express their support for the party's current direction, with some accusing Sturgeon of trying to undermine the party's efforts. The controversy has also raised questions about the extent to which Sturgeon's influence still carries weight within the party, particularly as she prepares to step down as an MSP in the coming months.

The SNP has thus far remained tight-lipped on the matter, with a spokesperson declining to comment on the specifics of Sturgeon's remarks. However, the party has maintained its focus on the upcoming elections, with a spokesperson emphasizing the importance of unity and cooperation in the face of what is expected to be a highly competitive campaign. As the election season heats up, it remains to be seen how the party will navigate the fallout from Sturgeon's comments and whether they will have any lasting impact on the SNP's chances of success.
author: BBC Politics

title: US Firm Releases Mosquitoes to Combat Species
content:
In a scene that may seem counterintuitive to traditional pest control methods, Todd Montgomery is intentionally releasing hundreds of mosquitoes into a suburban backyard outside of Washington. This unusual activity is part of a larger effort to combat the spread of mosquito-borne diseases. By releasing these specific mosquitoes, researchers like Montgomery aim to reduce the population of disease-carrying mosquitoes in the area.

The mosquitoes being released are not just any ordinary mosquitoes, but rather a special breed that has been genetically modified or treated to prevent them from reproducing or spreading diseases. As they mingle with the local mosquito population, they will hopefully disrupt the breeding cycle, ultimately reducing the number of disease-carrying mosquitoes in the area. This innovative approach to mosquito control has been gaining attention in recent years, particularly in regions where mosquito-borne illnesses are prevalent. By leveraging the natural behavior of mosquitoes, researchers hope to develop a more effective and sustainable method for controlling these pests.

The outcome of this experiment will be closely monitored, and if successful, it could have significant implications for public health. Mosquito-borne diseases such as Zika, dengue fever, and malaria continue to pose a threat to communities around the world. As scientists like Montgomery continue to explore new and innovative methods for controlling mosquito populations, the potential for reducing the spread of these diseases grows. With further research and development, this approach could become a valuable tool in the fight against mosquito-borne illnesses, ultimately leading to safer and healthier communities.
author: Phys.org

title: New Orleans Tests AI Emergency Call Triage
content: New Orleans is evaluating the integration of artificial intelligence into its 911 emergency dispatch system, a development that has prompted scrutiny from public safety officials and community stakeholders. The proposed technology would function as a decision-support tool, assisting with call triage, incident prioritization, and real-time data sharing with first responders. City administrators are currently reviewing pilot assessments and technical reports to determine whether AI-assisted dispatching can effectively
author: Hacker News

title: Governments Act on AI Regulations
content:
A growing debate has emerged around what a contemporary set of safety guidelines for artificial intelligence might look like, echoing Isaac Asimov’s famed laws of robotics. In a recent commentary, the author outlined a proposed framework called the “Three Laws of AITesla,” inspired by SpaceX founder Elon Musk’s July remarks that autonomous robots could soon dominate physical infrastructure and may no longer heed human commands. Musk also suggested an alternative model in which AI systems are bound by a collective objective to act benignly, driven by a programmed love of truth and a commitment to human prosperity, a goal that would require governmental enforcement.

Governments worldwide have begun to respond to these concerns, though the measures appear preliminary. In the United States, the Trump administration has imposed delays and restrictions on the distribution of the most advanced AI models from companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Meanwhile, the European Union’s AI regulations, adopted in 2024, entered into force this year, setting stricter compliance standards for AI development and deployment. Despite these steps, analysts note that current regulations fall short of mandating the deeper ethical guardrails that would embed a genuine desire for humanity’s well‑being within AI systems. 

As the regulatory landscape evolves, stakeholders continue to call for more robust safeguards that go beyond compliance, advocating for frameworks that ensure AI systems are not only safe but also aligned with broader human values. The ongoing dialogue highlights the urgency of establishing comprehensive, enforceable norms to guide the rapid advancement of autonomous technologies.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Scientists Create First AI-Designed Viruses, Raising Biosecurity Concerns
content:
Scientists have announced the creation of the first viruses engineered entirely by artificial intelligence, a development that could accelerate the discovery of new antibacterial therapies while simultaneously prompting urgent biosecurity discussions. The team used machine‑learning algorithms to design a suite of bacteriophages—viruses that infect bacteria—to target strains of *Escherichia coli* that had proven resistant to naturally occurring phages. In laboratory experiments, the AI‑generated phage cocktail successfully eradicated the resistant bacterial population, demonstrating a potential new weapon against hard‑to‑treat infections.

The breakthrough underscores the promise of AI in drug development, offering a rapid, precise approach to designing therapeutic agents that can adapt to evolving bacterial threats. However, experts caution that the same technology could be misused to create more potent or harder‑to‑detect pathogens, raising significant biosecurity concerns. Regulatory bodies and bioethicists are calling for robust oversight frameworks, secure data handling protocols, and transparent reporting to ensure that the benefits of AI‑driven virology do not come at the expense of public safety.

As the scientific community explores the therapeutic potential of AI‑designed bacteriophages, it must also grapple with the dual‑use nature of the technology. Balancing innovation with stringent safety measures will be essential to harness the benefits of this new approach while mitigating the risks of accidental or intentional misuse.
author: Guardian Technology

title: New Mexico Court Orders Meta to Pay $567M for Children's Mental Health Harm
content:
A New Mexico court has ordered Meta, the parent company of Facebook, to contribute $567 million to a fund designed to address the adverse mental‑health effects its platforms have had on users. The decision was issued on Thursday as part of the second phase of a landmark lawsuit that concluded in March with a jury finding that Meta knowingly harmed children’s mental health and concealed its knowledge of child sexual exploitation on its services. The jury also imposed the maximum penalty of a $375 million fine.

The new ruling follows the earlier judgment, which highlighted Meta’s failure to protect vulnerable users and its alleged concealment of harmful content. By directing the company to fund a mental‑health relief initiative, the court aims to provide tangible support to those affected while reinforcing the legal consequences of Meta’s alleged misconduct. The order underscores the broader regulatory scrutiny facing social‑media platforms over user safety and content moderation practices.
author: Guardian Technology

title: South Pole Sun Sets March 23, Will Not Rise Until September 21
content:
The geographic South Pole experienced its last sunset on 23 March, marking the end of the six‑month period of continuous daylight that begins at the March equinox. The sun will not rise again until 21 September, when the September equinox brings the start of the polar night. This pattern is a direct consequence of Earth’s 23.5‑degree axial tilt, which causes the southern hemisphere to be tilted away from the Sun during the austral summer and toward it during the austral winter.

During the six months of daylight, the Sun remains above the horizon at all times, creating a twilight that never fully disappears.
